title: postfix ! before an element access compiles and runs: element access was never the distinction
notes: RETIRED REFUSAL, kept under its old filename so the COVERAGE.md row that cites it (§4.14) keeps resolving. specification/failures.mdx §Refusal Conditions withdrew the placement walk; see DECISIONS.md §Typed failures. WHY IT NOW PASSES: `lookup("ada")!` is unconditional, once-evaluated, and has nothing effectful to its left, so its guard hoists to the front of the `const` and the emitted program evaluates `lookup`, checks, then indexes — the authored order. The old rule's distinction between a property access (admitted) and an element access (refused) was a property of its allow-list of seven node kinds and not of evaluation order, which is why it disappears rather than moving. The boundary approached from the other side is unchanged and still pinned elsewhere: specification/compatibility.mdx §Reinterpreted Syntax's `arr[i]!` is `!` APPLIED TO an element read, certified by 07-must-consume/an-array-literal-of-results-is-consumed-through-an-index-read. MARKER RETIRED 2026-08-30, and the fork's half of the withdrawal is what retired it. `safeUnwrapPlacement` and `isInRepeatedLoopHeader` are deleted from `compiler/forkbridge/lowering.go.txt` and replaced by the SAME three predicates the reference applies — `conditionallyEvaluatedPosition`, `repeatedlyEvaluatedPosition` and `precededByUnhoistedEffect` — so both backends now accept this program for the same stated reason. Re-derived by RUNNING both backends over this case, not by reading either one's source: the fork's predicates were written against measured behaviour and checked against the reference on the three programs that keep the residue alive (`while (next()!) {}`, `maybe ?? r!`, `g() + r!`), each of which both backends still refuse with the same code at the same position.
